abstract: Linking cellular phenotype to genotype and gene expression is a central goal in biomedical research. Live-cell imaging captures dynamic cellular phenotypes, whereas single-cell sequencing measures genome-wide molecular states, but pairing these readouts for the same cell remains challenging. Here we present Waldo, a genetically encoded single-cell barcoding strategy that can be read out by both live-cell imaging and single-cell sequencing to connect single cells across both modalities. Waldo barcodes are generated by combinatorial expression of synthetic cell-surface receptors, each detected by a cognate peptide probe coupled either to a fluorescent dye or a DNA barcode. Iterative fluorescent probe staining achieves large barcode diversity, while preserving fluorescence channels for phenotypic reporters. As a proof-of-principle, we use Waldo to link cell division phenotypes after chromosome missegregation to the karyotype and transcriptome of the same cells. Waldo provides a general strategy for connecting imaging phenotypes to genome-wide sequencing readouts in single cells.
